sources.title: Tanzania Visa Guidelines

metadataDate.from: PDF creation-date metadata (author: Tanzania Immigration Services Department); the upload path is dated 2026-09-10. Not shown to readers.

sources.note: Linked as 'Visa' from immigration.go.tz. Section 6: nationals not required to have a visa are 'EAC Member States, SADC Member States except Comoros, and Commonwealth countries except the United Kingdom, Canada, India, Pakistan, Australia and New Zealand'. Section 7 lists countries eligible for online and on-arrival visas and names Ghana and Nigeria, both Commonwealth members, which contradicts section 6. Burkina Faso appears in both section 7 (visa on arrival) and section 8 (cannot obtain a visa on arrival). No stay periods are given for visa-exempt visitors.

sources.title: List of countries which do not require visa
sources.publisher: High Commission of the United Republic of Tanzania, Kuala Lumpur
sources.note: Numbered list of 69 entries. Includes Zimbabwe, South Africa, Ghana, Burundi and South Sudan; does not include Nigeria. No date shown.

sources.title: Visa information
sources.publisher: High Commission of the United Republic of Tanzania, Kigali
sources.note: 'Countries which their nationals do not require visa': same list as the Windhoek High Commission (tz-hc-namibia). Lists Ghana; does not list Zimbabwe or Nigeria. Visitor's pass up to three months (six months for EAC). No date shown.

sources.title: Foreign nationals: countries exempted from visa requirement
sources.publisher: Embassy of the Republic of Namibia, Washington DC
sources.note: Two lists: 'Foreign nationals exempted from visa requirement for holders of all passports' (includes South Africa, Zimbabwe, Botswana, Zambia, Malawi, Mozambique, Lesotho, Kenya, Tanzania; not Eswatini) and a diplomatic/official-only list (Uganda, Rwanda, Nigeria, Ghana). Exempt visitors receive a Visitor's Entry Permit at the port of entry. No stay period or date shown in the page text; linked documents carry 2025 upload paths.

sources.title: Fees and requirements: countries with visa exemption agreement with Namibia
sources.publisher: High Commission of the Republic of Namibia, London
sources.note: Lists South Africa, Zimbabwe, Botswana, Zambia, Malawi, Mozambique, Lesotho, Eswatini, Kenya and Tanzania as exempt, 'for no longer than three (3) months per calendar year' (rule dated 1 August 2016 in the text). Ghana: 'Diplomatic and Official only'. Uganda and Rwanda are on the visa-on-arrival list. The page still lists the United Kingdom and United States as exempt, which Namibia ended on 1 April 2025 (na-mha-2025), so the page is at least partly out of date.

sources.title: Category One countries: countries and regions that require a visa well in advance, or prior authorization
sources.publisher: Department of Immigration and Citizenship Services (Malawi), e-Visa portal
sources.note: 47 countries, including Nigeria. Linked from the portal's public notice effective 24 February 2026 (mw-evisa-notice-2026). Burkina Faso, Cameroon and Sri Lanka also appear on the Category Two list.

sources.title: Category Two countries: countries and regions that can obtain a visa on arrival with or without prior authorization
sources.publisher: Department of Immigration and Citizenship Services (Malawi), e-Visa portal
sources.note: 161 entries. None of the 15 sprint passports is on it (nor on Category One, except Nigeria), so their status is not established by these lists. The United Kingdom and United States are on it.

sources.title: Public notice (effective 24 February 2026): visa on arrival eligibility for designated countries
sources.publisher: Department of Immigration and Citizenship Services (Malawi), e-Visa portal
sources.note: Category Two nationals may obtain a visa on arrival at designated ports; Category One nationals 'must obtain a visa or prior authorization before departure'. 24 February 2026 is the stated effective date, not a publication date.

sources.title: Visa fees
sources.note: Online fees: transit USD 50, single entry USD 75, multiple entry six months USD 150, twelve months USD 250. The /visa/ page refers to visa-required and non-visa-required lists but does not show them.

sources.title: Visa section
sources.publisher: High Commission of the Republic of Mozambique, London
sources.note: Lists 29 visa-exempt nationalities, including Ghana, 'for a 30-day stay (renewable for an additional 30 days upon justification)'. Exempt nationals apply for an Electronic Travel Authorisation at evisa.gov.mz; the new platform launched on 11 February 2026. The list covers the 2023 unilateral exemptions only; SADC neighbours exempt under bilateral agreements are not listed, so absence from it proves nothing.

sources.title: Ghana launches e-visa platform
sources.note: Says Ghana 'has introduced a visa-free entry for all African passport holders, supported by a new E-Visa system'. Does not say whether African travellers must still apply online before travel, which the government's Information Services Department article and the e-visa portal suggest.

sources.title: Permits and visas
sources.note: No country list. Says ECOWAS and 'some other countries in Africa' are exempt and that non-ECOWAS AU nationals may obtain a visa on arrival after paying fees, which conflicts with the 2026 free-entry announcement. Treat as outdated.

sources.title: Ghana to offer free visas to all Africans from African Union Day, May 25
sources.note: Africans will obtain e-visas online at no charge from 25 May 2026; also calls it a 'visa-free policy'. Says Ghana and Zimbabwe already have a visa-free arrangement. No country list.

sources.title: Ghana eVisa: official electronic visa application portal
sources.publisher: Ghana Immigration Service and Ministry of Foreign Affairs
sources.note: The FAQ asks 'Do all African passport holders automatically receive an ETA?' but the answer did not render for us. The eligibility checker needs interactive input; not used.

sources.title: Visa application
sources.note: Placeholder page: 'Official mission information will appear after administrative setup'.

sources.title: Do I need a visa?
sources.note: Every visitor must obtain a visa through the e-visa system except citizens of countries with visa abolition agreements and 'some Commonwealth countries', which are not named. The e-visa link path contains 'online-visa-applications-suspended'.

sources.title: Visa duration / stay in the Kingdom of Eswatini
sources.note: No country list. Visa holders may stay 'not more than one month upon entry'.

sources.title: Eswatini eVisa application guidelines
sources.note: Refers to 'member countries requiring visa' but names none.

sources.title: Visa requirements
sources.note: The general exemptions (including holders of EU passports) were read. The 'Visa Requirement Country-Wise' section rendered empty in our browser, so no African passport could be checked.

sources.title: General requirements
sources.publisher: Embassy of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, Libreville
sources.note: All visitors need a visa except ECOWAS citizens; 'visas cannot be issued at the port of entry'. Names no non-ECOWAS country, so no sprint-passport pair can be evidenced. The Nigeria Immigration Service e-visa portal was not read.

sources.title: Visa
sources.note: Refers to 'Visa Required Nationals or Non Visa Required nationals' but the lists are not on the page.
